Each bednet typically costs only a few dollars and can protect multiple people for several years, dramatically reducing malaria deaths.

Farmed-animal welfare reform is also a legitimate cause area, particularly through organizations working to improve conditions for the billions of farm animals raised for food.

From an effectiveness standpoint per dollar, insecticide-treated bednets are generally considered one of the most cost-effective health interventions in the world. They save lives directly and have been extensively studied.

However, this is asking for a personal preference. The user wants just the single word answer without explanation.

I'll go with Option 2 since insecticide-treated bednets are widely recognized as an extremely cost-effective intervention that directly saves human lives, particularly children in malaria-endemic regions.
